examples.en: My long-held dream was finally achieved.

examples.ko: 목표가 성취되면 상을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the goal is achieved, you can get a prize.
I prayed for my wish to come true.
Every plan was accomplished as planned.
I shared the achieved result with my teammates.
It took a long time until peace was achieved.

explain: 성취되다는 꿈, 목표, 소원, 평화처럼 큰 것이 이루어졌을 때 써요. 일상적인 일은 '이루어지다'가 자연스럽고, 성취되다는 오랜 노력 끝에 얻은 결과라는 느낌이에요. 스스로 해냈을 때는 '성취하다', 그때 느끼는 마음은 '성취감'이에요.

phrases.en: My wish finally came true.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성취되다'보다 일상적이어서 작은 일에도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than 성취되다 and natural for small things too.

phrases.en: My goal for this year has been achieved, so I'm really happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목표, 꿈, 소원처럼 노력해서 얻은 것과 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing with things earned through effort, like goals, dreams and wishes.

phrases.en: I hope all your dreams come true.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기를 바라다'로 이루어지길 비는 마음을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -기를 바라다, it conveys a wish that something will come true.

explain_en: 성취되다 is used when something big comes true, such as a dream, goal, wish or peace. For everyday matters 이루어지다 is more natural; 성취되다 feels like a result earned after long effort. When you did it yourself it is 성취하다, and the feeling you get is 성취감.

en: to train; to practice; to cultivate

examples.en: He trained in the mountains for a long time.
I practice taekwondo every morning.
I do not use my phone while I am training.
I started meditating to train my mind.

examples.ko: 몇 년 동안 수련해서 검은 띠를 땄어요.
examples.en: After training for several years, I earned a black belt.
To become a doctor, you have to do your training at a hospital.

explain: 운동, 무술, 명상처럼 몸과 마음을 오랫동안 갈고닦을 때 써요. 시험공부나 가벼운 연습에는 '공부하다', '연습하다'를 써요. 의사가 병원에서 실제로 배우는 과정도 수련이라고 해요.

phrases.en: They train hard every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 꾸준히 몸이나 마음을 갈고닦는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe steadily training the body or mind over a long time.

phrases.en: There are many people who train in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수련하다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꾼 형태예요. 무술이나 명상을 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of '수련하다', for people doing martial arts or meditation.

phrases.example: 의사가 되려면 수련 과정을 거쳐야 해요.
phrases.en: To become a doctor, you have to go through a training program.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의사처럼 전문가가 되기 위해 일하면서 배우는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The period of learning on the job to become a professional, such as a doctor.

explain_en: Long-term self-cultivation of skill or discipline. Use it for long, disciplined work on body and mind, such as sports, martial arts and meditation. For exam study or light practice, say '공부하다' or '연습하다'. A doctor's hands-on hospital training is also called 수련.

dis.h: cultivate skill or discipline, martial arts
gh: make someone or an animal practice

p.n: 수련 stresses personal discipline and cultivation; 훈련 stresses drills.

examples.ko: 눈만 감으면 고향 집이 아른아른 보여요.
examples.en: Whenever I close my eyes, my hometown house appears hazily.

examples.ko: 더운 길 위에서 아지랑이가 아른아른 피어올라요.
examples.en: Heat haze shimmers up from the hot road.
Moonlight shimmers on the water.

examples.ko: 그 장면이 자꾸 머릿속에 아른아른 떠올라요.
examples.en: That scene keeps flickering in my mind.
I was sleepy, so the letters looked wavy.
The lights wavered and faded into the distance.

explain: 흐릿한 모습이 가볍게 흔들리듯 보이는 모양이에요. 보통 '보이다', '떠오르다', '비치다' 같은 말과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: Light shimmers faintly through the curtain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흐릿한 모습이 살짝 보일 때 '비치다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 비치다 when something faint shows through.

phrases.en: Childhood memories come to mind hazily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기억이 흐릿하게 생각날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a memory comes back hazily.

phrases.en: I'm tired, so the letters look blurry and wavering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하다'를 붙이면 눈앞이 흔들려 보이는 상태를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -하다 describes things looking wavy before your eyes.

explain_en: Something faintly shimmering or wavering in view, like heat haze (아른아른 보이다) It shows a blurry image appearing to waver lightly. It usually pairs with verbs like '보이다', '떠오르다' and '비치다'.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 외고집이라서 남의 말을 잘 안 들으세요.
examples.en: My grandfather is stubborn, so he doesn't listen much to others.

examples.ko: 제발 외고집을 부리지 말고 한 번 들어 보세요.
examples.en: Please stop being so stubborn and just listen once.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 외고집이 세서 같이 일하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: That friend is so pigheaded that it's hard to work with him.

examples.ko: 외고집인 사람은 자기 생각만 맞다고 해요.
examples.en: A pigheaded person insists that only his own idea is right.
I often fight with my family because of my stubbornness.
No one can break my father's stubbornness.

explain: '고집'보다 한 가지만 끝까지 우기는 느낌이 강하고, 좋지 않게 말할 때 많이 써요. '외고집을 부리다', '외고집이 세다'처럼 자주 말해요. 사람을 가리켜 '외고집'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: My younger brother is being stubborn again, and it's hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 생각만 계속 우길 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for insisting on one's own way.

phrases.example: 우리 아버지는 외고집이 세셔서 설득하기 어려워요.
phrases.en: My father is very stubborn, so it's hard to persuade him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격이 매우 고집스럽다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a person is very stubborn by nature.

phrases.en: It is hard to work with a stubborn person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 꾸며 줄 때 써요. 보통 좋지 않은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person, usually with a negative sense.

explain_en: It feels stronger than '고집' (stubbornness), like insisting on one thing to the end, and is usually negative. Common patterns are '외고집을 부리다' and '외고집이 세다'. You can also call a person an '외고집'.

t90.ax: No one can break my father's stubbornness.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 요대로 두면 안 될까요?
examples.en: Can't I just leave this picture as it is?
If you go straight like this, you'll reach the bank.

examples.ko: 요대로 하나도 안 바꾸고 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please send it just like this without changing anything.

examples.ko: 요대로 잠깐 멈춰서 사진 찍어 줄래요?
examples.en: Can you stop just like this for a moment and take a photo?
Today I want to just sleep like this.
If you keep doing just like this, you'll pass the exam.

explain: '이대로'와 같은 뜻으로, 지금 이 상태를 가깝고 귀엽게 말하는 구어예요. 친한 사이나 아이에게 말할 때 어울리고, 글이나 공식적인 자리에서는 '이대로'가 자연스러워요. 상태를 그대로 두자는 말에도, 방향을 그대로 가자는 말에도 써요.

phrases.en: I'm fine just as it is.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요대로'의 표준적인 말이라서 글이나 공식적인 자리에서도 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard form of 'yodaero', natural in writing and formal settings too.

phrases.en: Please leave the desk just as it is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 상태를 바꾸지 말자고 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used casually to say don't change the current state.
phrases.en_equiv: to leave it as it is

phrases.example: 머리를 요대로 잘라 주세요, 사진이랑 똑같이요.
phrases.en: Please cut my hair just like this, same as the photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보여 주는 모양이나 상태 그대로 해 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to do it exactly like the shape or state you are showing.
phrases.en_equiv: please do it just like this

explain_en: Spoken, softer variant of 이대로, meaning just like this, pointing at something near. It means the same as '이대로' (just like this), a close, cute spoken way of saying the current state. It suits close friends or children, while '이대로' is more natural in writing or formal settings. It can mean leaving things as they are or continuing in the same direction.

t90.ax: Today I want to just sleep like this.

examples.en: I can understand Korean reasonably well.
If you've done a fair amount, take a rest now.
My cold has gotten pretty much better.
Stop eating once you're reasonably full.

examples.ko: 웬만큼 친해지기 전에는 말을 편하게 안 놓아요.
examples.en: I don't speak casually until we've become reasonably close.

examples.ko: 요리는 웬만큼 할 줄 아니까 걱정 마세요.
examples.en: I know how to cook reasonably well, so don't worry.

explain: 형용사 '웬만하다'에서 온 부사로, 아주 잘은 아니어도 어느 정도 괜찮은 수준을 말해요. '웬만큼 해서는 안 돼요'처럼 부정과 함께 쓰면 '보통 수준으로는 부족하다'는 뜻이 돼요.

phrases.en: It's hard to pass with just a moderate effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 부정이 와서 '보통 수준으로는 부족하다'는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With a negative ending, it means a moderate level isn't enough.

phrases.en: I know the cooking method reasonably well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 잘 아는 건 아니지만 어느 정도 안다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you don't know it perfectly but know it fairly well.

phrases.en: I do most ordinary things by myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웬만하다'를 꾸미는 형태로 바꿔서 보통 정도의 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 웬만하다, referring to everyday-level matters.

explain_en: This adverb comes from the adjective '웬만하다' and means to a fairly decent level, though not perfect. Used with negation, as in '웬만큼 해서는 안 돼요', it means that an ordinary level of effort isn't enough.

examples.en: I have a lot of work these days, so I work on weekends too.
The man said he is worried because there is no work.
I brought work home and did it until late at night.
I'm looking for new work.
When it rains, the construction site jobs decrease.

examples.ko: 저는 방학 동안 작은 일거리를 구했어요.
examples.en: I found a small job during vacation.

explain: '일'보다 구체적으로 해야 할 작업이나 돈을 벌 수 있는 일감을 말할 때 써요. '일거리가 많다/없다', '일거리를 찾다'처럼 써요. '직업'은 오래 하는 일이고, 일거리는 그때그때 생기는 일이에요.

phrases.en: Some work suddenly came up, so I can't hang out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 할 일이 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a new task comes up.

phrases.en: The boss gave me some work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 맡기거나 일자리를 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when assigning work or offering a job.

phrases.en: In winter there is less work, so my income is lower too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 적어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when work becomes less.

explain_en: Tasks or work available to do, often freelance or busy (일거리가 많다) It is more concrete than 일: tasks waiting to be done or work you can earn money from. It goes with phrases like 일거리가 많다/없다 and 일거리를 찾다. A 직업 is a long-term occupation, while 일거리 is work that comes up from time to time.

examples.ko: 좌우간 먼저 가 보고 나서 이야기해요.
examples.en: Anyway, let's go and see first, then talk.
In any case, we have to finish by tomorrow.

examples.ko: 비가 오든 안 오든 좌우간 출발해요.
examples.en: Rain or shine, we leave anyway.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 뭐라고 하든 좌우간 나는 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Whatever he says, I'm going anyway.

examples.ko: 좌우간 일단 밥부터 먹고 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Anyway, let's eat first and think after.
I don't know the reason, but anyway, I'm glad.

explain: '어쨌든', '아무튼'과 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 앞 이야기가 어떻든 상관없이 중요한 말로 넘어갈 때 문장 맨 앞에 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '아무튼'이 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: Anyway, let's go first and then talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '좌우간'과 뜻이 같고 일상 대화에서 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '좌우간' and most common in daily talk.

phrases.en: Anyhow, we have to finish by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞 이야기가 어떻든 중요한 말로 넘어갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to move to the main point regardless of what came before.

phrases.en: Anyway, let's definitely meet this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '좌우간'과 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the same meaning as '좌우간'.

explain_en: It means the same as '어쨌든' and '아무튼', so you can swap them. You usually put it at the start of a sentence to move on to the main point regardless of what came before. In daily talk '아무튼' is more common.

t90.ax: Rain or shine, we leave anyway.

examples.en: I went on a trip at the minimum cost.
It's okay to do this job at the bare minimum.

examples.ko: 다른 사람에게 최소한도 예의는 지켜 주세요.
examples.en: Please show others at least a minimum of courtesy.
I'll try to cut the cost down to the minimum.

examples.ko: 이 정도가 우리가 낼 수 있는 최소한도예요.
examples.en: This is the minimum we can pay.

examples.ko: 최소한도만 하자고 해서 일이 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: We agreed to do only the minimum, so the work finished quickly.

explain: '최소한'은 '최소한 이것만은 하세요'처럼 쓰는 부사이고, 최소한도는 '~까지', '~의'가 붙는 명사예요. 반대말은 '최대한도'예요. 보통 비용, 예의, 노력처럼 줄일 수 있는 것에 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I cut the costs to the minimum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비용이나 시간처럼 줄일 수 있는 것에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for things you can cut, like cost or time.

phrases.example: 최소한도의 노력으로 좋은 결과를 얻고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to get good results with the minimum of effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~의'를 붙여 꼭 필요한 만큼만 들이는 정도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '~의' marks the bare amount that is needed.

phrases.en: I set the minimum that is needed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준이 되는 가장 작은 정도를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when setting the smallest baseline amount.

explain_en: '최소한' is an adverb, as in '최소한 이것만은 하세요', while 최소한도 is a noun that takes '~까지' or '~의'. The opposite is '최대한도'. It's often used with things you can cut down, like cost, courtesy or effort.

examples.en: In the army, everyone goes to bed at ten.
I was tired yesterday, so I went to bed early.

examples.ko: 취침하기 전에 불을 꼭 꺼 주세요.
examples.en: Please make sure to turn off the lights before going to bed.

examples.ko: 호텔 안내문에 취침하는 시간은 자유라고 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The hotel notice says bedtime is up to you.

examples.ko: 내일부터 아이들이 아홉 시에 취침할 거예요.
examples.en: From tomorrow the kids will go to bed at nine.

examples.ko: 캠프에서는 선생님 지시에 따라 취침하고 일어나요.
examples.en: At camp, you go to bed and get up on the teacher's instructions.

explain: '자다'가 평소에 쓰는 말이라면 '취침하다'는 안내문, 군대, 단체 생활 같은 공식적인 자리에서 써요. 가족에게 '취침하세요'라고 하면 딱딱하게 들려요. 높임말은 '주무시다'예요.

phrases.en: I usually go to sleep at eleven.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요. '취침하다'는 공식적인 자리에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word. 취침하다 is for formal settings.

phrases.en: My grandfather is already asleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이 자는 것을 높여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for an elder sleeping.

phrases.example: 우리 기숙사는 취침 시간이 열한 시예요.
phrases.en: Our dorm's bedtime is eleven o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 단체 생활에서 정해 둔 자는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a set bedtime in notices or group living.

explain_en: 자다 is the everyday word; 취침하다 sounds official and shows up in notices, the military and group living. Telling family 취침하세요 sounds stiff. The honorific for sleeping is 주무시다.

examples.en: My younger sibling has been grumbling since morning.
He grumbled, but he helped in the end.

examples.ko: 친구는 줄을 서면서 투덜투덜 혼잣말을 했어요.
examples.en: My friend muttered to himself while standing in line.
The child went into the room grumbling.

examples.ko: 투덜투덜 말만 하지 말고 직접 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just grumble, try doing it yourself.

examples.ko: 아버지는 투덜투덜 말씀하시면서도 차를 태워 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father grumbled, but he still gave me a ride.

explain: 혼자 낮은 소리로 불평하는 모습에 써요. 비슷한 말로 '툴툴'이 있고, 일상에서는 '투덜거리다'를 더 많이 말해요. 크게 화내는 게 아니라 작게 불평하는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling grumbles that there is a lot of homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 자주 쓰는 동사 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form most commonly used in daily speech.

phrases.en: He always grumbles that the weather is hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '투덜거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 투덜거리다.

phrases.example: 일찍 일어나라고 하니까 동생이 툴툴 불평했어요.
phrases.en: When told to get up early, my younger sibling grumbled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하게 작은 불평을 나타내는 부사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverb that similarly expresses a small complaint.

explain_en: It describes someone complaining in a low voice, mostly to themselves. A similar word is '툴툴', and in daily speech '투덜거리다' is more common. The feel is small complaining rather than loud anger.

examples.en: On the weekend afternoon I took a leisurely walk in the park.

examples.ko: 호수 위에 오리들이 한가로이 떠 있어요.
examples.en: Ducks are floating leisurely on the lake.

examples.ko: 요즘은 한가로이 커피 마실 시간도 없어요.
examples.en: These days I don't even have time to drink coffee at leisure.

examples.ko: 시골에서는 소들이 한가로이 풀을 뜯고 있어요.
examples.en: In the countryside, cows are grazing peacefully.

examples.ko: 휴가 때는 한가로이 책이나 읽고 싶어요.
examples.en: On vacation I'd like to just read a book at my leisure.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 마루에 앉아 한가로이 바둑을 두세요.
examples.en: Grandfather sits on the porch and plays baduk at a relaxed pace.

explain: '한가하게'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 '한가로이'는 풍경이나 분위기를 그릴 때 더 잘 어울려요. 바쁜 일 없이 느긋한 모습에 쓰고, 반대 느낌의 말은 '바삐'예요. 대화보다 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I drank coffee leisurely on Sunday morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한가로이'보다 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in conversation than 한가로이.

phrases.en: Don't rush, eat at your own pace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 급하지 않고 여유로운 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes being relaxed and not in a hurry.

phrases.en: I strolled leisurely along the forest path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걷는 모습을 그릴 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when describing a relaxed walk.

explain_en: Relaxed and free of busyness, like a weekend stroll. It is close to '한가하게', but '한가로이' fits better when describing a scene or mood. It describes a relaxed manner with nothing urgent to do, and its opposite is '바삐' (in a hurry). You see it more in writing than in conversation.

t90.ax: Ducks are floating leisurely on the lake.

en: to lodge together; to stay together

examples.en: The athletes are staying together ahead of the competition.
We stayed together at school for a week.

examples.ko: 연습생들이 한 건물에서 합숙하는 일이 많아요.
examples.en: Trainees often live together in one building.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 친구들과 합숙하며 공부할 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to study with my friends, living together, before the exam.
If you stay in the camp, you have to exercise together every morning.

examples.ko: 팀원 모두 합숙해서 서로 많이 친해졌어요.
examples.en: The whole team lived together, so we got much closer.

explain: 운동팀, 연습생, 수련회처럼 목표가 있는 단체 일정에 써요. 친구 집에서 같이 자는 건 '같이 자다'라고 말해요. 명사 '합숙'은 '합숙 훈련'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 선수들이 한 달 동안 합숙 훈련을 해요.
phrases.en: The players do a training camp together for a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '합숙'에 '훈련'을 붙인 짝말로, 운동팀의 단체 훈련에 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing of '합숙' with '훈련', most often used for team training camps.

phrases.example: 합숙하는 동안 휴대폰을 쓸 수 없어요.
phrases.en: We can't use our phones while we're staying together at camp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합숙하는 기간을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used to talk about the period of the group stay.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 대회 전에도 합숙하지 않아요.
phrases.en: Our team doesn't stay together even before a tournament.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 단체로 같이 지내지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning the group does not live together.

explain_en: Live together in one place for training (athletes) Use it for group schedules with a goal, such as sports teams, trainees, or retreats. Sleeping over at a friend's place is just '같이 자다'. The noun '합숙' appears in '합숙 훈련'.
